::: {.bs-lesson-preamble}
NICE is a repeatable engineering design cycle for moving from a problem to evidence, reflection, and a better next version.
:::

## N: Needs & Necessities

Define what the design must do.

A **need** is a minimum condition the design must satisfy. A **necessity** is something important that improves the solution, but can be prioritized or traded against other considerations.

Record requirements so they can be tested later.

## I: Investigate & Inquire

Ask questions before committing to a solution.

Research existing approaches, investigate materials and processes, identify constraints, collect measurements, test assumptions, and record useful evidence.

## C: Create & Communicate

Generate possible solutions, choose a direction, and make the idea testable.

Depending on the project, this can include sketches, CAD, code, schematics, calculations, prototypes, fabricated parts, photos, demonstrations, and technical explanations.

## E: Evaluate

Compare the result with the original needs and necessities.

Record what worked, what failed, what evidence supports the conclusion, and what should change next.

## Keep the cycle moving

NICE is not a one-way checklist.

**N -> I -> C -> E -> N**

Evaluation creates new information. That information changes the next set of needs, questions, and design decisions.
